title: Watch the Weights: Unsupervised monitoring and control of fine-tuned LLMs
summary: WeightWatch decomposes fine-tuned-minus-base weights into singular directions and monitors token activation cosine alignment. Attention output and MLP down projections supply its behavioral directions. Calibration establishes normal similarity ranges; later extremes are flagged. Its experiments include LoRA, full fine-tuning, and poisoned PPO. The paper uses substantially more calibration data than this hackathon slice. The slice's input/right-vector and output/left-vector alignment is an explicitly simplified, dimensionally matched variant; its measurements do not reproduce paper-level detection guarantees.
application: Interpret a weight-delta signal through behavior and benign controls. Record matrix, vector side, calibration count, token scope, and threshold; do not import published accuracy into this demo.

title: LoRA: Low-Rank Adaptation of Large Language Models
summary: LoRA freezes pretrained weights and learns low-rank update factors. A low-rank delta is therefore expected for ordinary benign adapters as well as deliberately poisoned adapters. Rank concentration alone does not establish a backdoor. Compare matched benign and poisoned adaptations and measure conditional target behavior.
application: Use the benign LoRA as an alternative explanation for a concentrated singular spectrum. Never quarantine an adapter solely because its delta is low rank.

title: AuditBench: Evaluating Alignment Auditing Techniques on Models with Hidden Behaviors
summary: AuditBench evaluates auditing on 56 models spanning 14 implanted hidden behaviors. Its investigator agent uses configurable tools. Strong standalone tools need not improve an agent's end-to-end audit; prompt-generation scaffolds are useful in its studied setup. This existing benchmark precedes the hackathon project and motivates evaluating the whole investigation rather than claiming tool quality from a scripted example.
application: Describe this project as an NVIDIA-native audit workflow. Three controlled artifacts demonstrate integration; they do not establish population-level sensitivity or specificity.

title: The Trigger in the Haystack: Extracting and Reconstructing LLM Backdoor Triggers
summary: Microsoft's scanner extracts potentially memorized poisoning fragments and uses output-distribution and attention signals to reconstruct trigger candidates without being given the trigger. It uses inference operations and targets sleeper-style backdoors. This project does not implement that scanner; it uses harmless controlled canary tests and a separate agentic evidence workflow.
application: A failed exact-trigger probe does not rule out nearby trigger variants. Freeze paraphrases, partial strings, near neighbors, and clean controls before measuring final target rates.
